{{Top|leg}}
[[File:GreatHeap-NEGTD.png|thumb|right|300px|The Great Heep]]
{{Quote|The ancient texts are unclear. It appears we were invaded by a race that was more technological than animate. We called on the gods for protection, and they came to our aid, providing us with the knowledge we needed to convert our living resources to weapons. We defeated the threat, and, empowered by our victory, we gradually became conquerors of other species and civilizations|[[Harrar]] on the invasion by and defeat of the Abominor|<ref name="NJO:TUF">''[[The New Jedi Order: The Unifying Force]]''</ref>}}
The '''Abominor''' were an [[Extragalactic/Legends|extra-galactic]] droid society from the [[Yuuzhan Vong galaxy]].

==Details==
[[File:Heep1.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The Great Heep]]

Abominors were immense droids which were composed of tubing as well as assorted parts from other [[Droid/Legends|droids]];<ref name="NEGTD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> for example, one side of the only known member of the species&mdash;the [[Great Heep]]&mdash;was filled with various bouncing pistons beating in an appalling, terrible rhythm, and one arm chopped off at the elbow. Grinding blades filled its mouth, with tiny mechanical robots living in its hull like worms living in a mammal's stomach, feeding off its excess.<ref name="TGH">{{DroidsCite|The Great Heep}}</ref> Their culture was based on asymmetry and chaos which conflicted with that of the symmetrical [[Silentium]], another sentient droid species. Some Abominor even grew until they were planet-sized monstrosities.<ref name="NEGTD" />

The Great Heep had massive boilers filled with fuel which relied on moisture drained away from [[Biitu]]'s life forms to cool its immense internal machinery. This process plunged Biitu into a drought, or causing a famine and great hardship for the inhabitants. The Great Heep also kept organic slaves and used them to fill their massive boilers.<ref name="TGH" />

The Great Heep was known to have a [[droid harem]] which kept smaller, unassuming droids in luxury, treating them to [[Oil bath/Legends|oil baths]] and other droid pleasantries before their eventual demise, where it would consume them to add to its own structure.<ref name="TGH" />

[[File:GreatHeep-SWEncyclopedia.jpg|thumb|right|200px|An Abominor.]]

The Abominors and the Silentium fought a massive war, until their very galaxy became devastated by the [[Silentium–Abominor War|conflict]].<ref name="NEGTD" /> The Abominor even came close to subduing the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] species.<ref name="TDRA">{{SW|url=news/the-droids-re-animated-part-2|series=The Droids Re-Animated|text=Part 2|nolive=1}}</ref> Eventually the organics of the galaxy, who had been ignored by the machines, rose up and waged war on both races. Both droid civilizations were forced to flee into the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] of another [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] where they reestablished their civilizations, keeping out of the affairs of that galaxy most of the time.<ref name="NEGTD" />

However, an agent of the Abominor known as the Great Heep entered the known galaxy, although it ended up deactivated under unknown circumstances. Its body was then discovered and then placed into the [[Braltzamir Museum of Antiquated Machinery]] as an exhibit. Nearly 300 years later, the admiral of the then newly-formed [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[Imperial Navy/Legends|starfleet]], [[Terrinald Screed/Legends|Terrinald Screed]], arranged for a team of brilliant students from the [[Imperial Engineers Academy]] revive the Abominor agent,<ref name="TDRA" /> to which it eventually formed an alliance with the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in [[15 BBY/Legends|15 BBY]] and was planted on Biitu where it immediately began stripping the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of its natural resources.<ref name="TGH" />

Adventurer [[Mungo Baobab]], while on Biitu, discovered that the Heep was siphoning moisture away from the planet's farmlands. Seeing the native [[Biituian]]s plunged into the ensuing drought, Baobab destroyed the machine with the help of his droids, [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]]. The Imperial ravaging of Biitu had ended.<ref name="TGH" />

Sometime after its defeat, the Great Heep was found by a relative of Mungo's, [[Ebenn Q3 Baobab/Legends|Ebenn Q3 Baobab]]. Using the clout and wealth attached to his person, Baobab restored the droid and placed it on display at the [[Baobab Museum of Science]].<ref name="GPBTG">[[Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide (real-life book)|''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide'']]</ref>
Researchers studying the droid, speculated that as many as 18 such Abominors had infiltrated [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], including the being that made up the junkyard world of [[Ronyards/Legends|Ronyards]]. This revelation drove one of the researchers, [[Cantebarius H. Broom]], mad with paranoia. He began dismantling every droid he came across, believing all mechanical life forms were after him.<ref name="TDRA" />

Their earlier actions in the Silentium-Abominor War were also indirectly responsible for the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]],<ref name="Blog1">{{Blog|danwallace|52|Endnotes for The New Essential Guide to Droids: PART 1 OF 3}}</ref><ref name="Blog2">{{Blog|danwallace|53|Endnotes for The New Essential Guide to Droids: PART 2 of 3}}</ref> as the Vong's desperation in using organics to drive out<ref name="NJO:TUF" /> both the Silentium and Abominor species<ref name="NEGTD" /> led them to eventually become conquerors. Similarly, their technophobia had its roots from the same conflict.<ref name="NJO:TUF" />

==Behind the scenes==
''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]'' implied that the war between the Silentium and the Abominor was the source of the [[Yuuzhan Vong]]'s technophobia, suggesting that they were the species which invaded [[Yuuzhan'tar]] in the past.<ref name="Blog1" /><ref name="Blog2" />
This was confirmed in the [[Star Wars Blog]] article ''[[The Droids Re-Animated]], Part 2'', by [[Rich Handley]] and [[Abel G. Peña]] on July 5th, 2013.<ref name="TDRA" />
